title: The rāsa-līlā in the Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Purāṇa and Bhāgavata
subject: narr:rasa-lila
question: How does each text tell Kṛṣṇa's nocturnal dance with the gopīs?

rows.statement: Short erotic description: on autumn nights Kṛṣṇa delights the young cowherd women, who sing his deeds in rows and pairs, imitate him and cling to him; no flute, no disappearance, no search, and the constituted text does not use the word rāsa (63.25, 63.35 'adorned with circles of gopīs').

Kṛṣṇa's song draws the gopīs; he vanishes; they act out his deeds and follow his footprints and those of a favoured gopī; he reappears and forms the rāsa-maṇḍala, holding each gopī by the hand; the chapter closes by declaring him the all-pervading Self.

sources.edition: Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner

rows.statement: Five chapters: the flute call, Kṛṣṇa's test of the gopīs, his disappearance at their pride, the search and footprints of one favoured gopī, the Gopī-gīta, the reunion, and the rāsa with Kṛṣṇa multiplied between each pair of women (10.33.3); Parīkṣit asks how the upholder of dharma could do this (10.33.26–37).
Reproduces the Viṣṇu Purāṇa account almost verbatim (rāsa-goṣṭhī, rāsa-maṇḍala).

sources.edition: Brahmapurāṇa 1–246, Tübingen Purāṇa Project (P. Schreiner, R. Söhnen-Thieme); GRETIL e-text

note: The sequence HV → ViP → BhP is generally read as successive elaboration (Hardy 1983; Schweig 2005); the Brahma Purāṇa copies the ViP. The named favourite, Rādhā, is absent from all four.

title: Where the Syamantaka jewel came from and how long Kṛṣṇa fought Jāmbavān
subject: narr:syamantaka
question: Who first obtained the jewel, from where, and how long did the fight with Jāmbavān last?

rows.statement: Prasena obtained the jewel 'from the ocean' as Dvāravatī was being founded; the story of the Sun giving it to Satrājit is a star (inserted) passage after 28.12. Kṛṣṇa fought Jāmbavān in the cave 'with his arms alone' for twenty-one days.
The Sun (Vivasvat) takes the jewel from his own neck and gives it to his friend Satrājit; the fight lasts twenty-one days.

sources.edition: Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner

rows.statement: Prasena(jit) obtained it 'from the Sun' (sūryād), with the Sun episode in the constituted text.

sources.edition: Brahmapurāṇa 1–246, Tübingen Purāṇa Project (P. Schreiner, R. Söhnen-Thieme); GRETIL e-text
sources.quote: divyaṃ syamantakaṃ nāma sa sūryād upalabdhavān

rows.statement: The Sun, pleased with Satrājit, gives him the jewel; Kṛṣṇa and Jāmbavān fight for twenty-eight days (aṣṭā-viṃśa-aham), and Jāmbavān recognises his lord Rāma; in 10.83.10 Jāmbavatī says twenty-seven days.

note: The critical Harivaṃśa's 'from the ocean' reading versus the Sun-gift in the Viṣṇu, Brahma and Bhāgavata Purāṇas suggests the solar origin entered with later redaction; the HV vulgate includes it.

title: Order and form of Kṛṣṇa's infant exploits
subject: char:krishna
question: Which infancy episodes does each text tell, and in what form?

rows.statement: Cart overturned (50.4–19), then Pūtanā as a night-bird (50.20–24); then the binding to the mortar and the twin trees (51). No Tṛṇāvarta, Agha or Brahmā episode.
Pūtanā (5.5), then the cart (5.6.1–8), the binding and the trees (5.6.9–20). No Tṛṇāvarta.

sources.edition: Critical edition, M. M. Pathak (Vadodara 1997–99); GRETIL e-text by P. Schreiner

rows.statement: Pūtanā (10.6), the cart and Tṛṇāvarta (10.7), butter-stealing and the universe in Kṛṣṇa's mouth (10.8), the binding (10.9) and the cursed yakṣas (10.10), then Vatsa, Baka (10.11), Agha (10.12) and Brahmā's theft (10.13–14).
Lists Pūtanā, the twin arjunas and the cart, then Kāliya, in a brief digest.

sources.edition: Rajendralal Mitra ed. (Bibliotheca Indica 1870–79); GRETIL e-text
